es: Reconocer cómo se estructura una historia para inspirar, advertir o convencer, señalar el momento que revela su propósito e inferir la postura del narrador.

vocabulary.es: relato con moraleja, historia de advertencia
dejar clara la idea, remachar el mensaje

teaching.en: A compelling story has an arc: a situation, a problem, a turning point and an outcome, and the audience waits for the last part with growing curiosity.
teaching.es: Una historia cautivadora tiene un arco: una situación, un problema, un giro y un desenlace, y la audiencia espera la última parte con curiosidad creciente.
teaching.explanationEs: Arc es la forma de la historia; outcome es cómo termina; compelling = difícil de dejar de escuchar.
segments: A compelling story has an arc: a situation, a problem, a turning point and
an outcome, and the audience waits for the last part with growing curiosity.
teaching.audioText: A compelling story has an arc: a situation, a problem, a turning point and an outcome, and the audience waits for the last part with growing curiosity.

teaching.en: A story can inspire: the speaker fails twice, then finds a way, and the audience leaves with more hope than it brought into the room.
teaching.es: Una historia puede inspirar: el narrador fracasa dos veces, luego encuentra un camino y la audiencia sale con más esperanza de la que trajo.
teaching.explanationEs: Inspire busca una emoción positiva; audience es el público que escucha.
segments: A story can inspire: the speaker fails twice, then finds a way, and
the audience leaves with more hope than it brought into the room.
teaching.audioText: A story can inspire: the speaker fails twice, then finds a way, and the audience leaves with more hope than it brought into the room.

teaching.en: A cautionary tale is meant to warn: it shows a mistake and its price, as in 'I ignored the noise, and the car stopped on a dark road.'
teaching.es: Un relato con moraleja está hecho para advertir: muestra un error y su precio, como en «Ignoré el ruido y el auto se paró en una carretera oscura».
teaching.explanationEs: Warn = avisar de un peligro; lo que importa es el error y lo que cuesta.
segments: A cautionary tale is meant to warn: it shows a mistake and its price,
as in 'I ignored the noise, and the car stopped on a dark road.'
teaching.audioText: A cautionary tale is meant to warn: it shows a mistake and its price, as in 'I ignored the noise, and the car stopped on a dark road.'

teaching.en: A story can also persuade, because the listener sees the result instead of hearing an argument: 'Our shop nearly closed, until one change saved it.'
teaching.es: Una historia también puede convencer, porque el oyente ve el resultado en lugar de oír un argumento: «Nuestra tienda casi cierra, hasta que un cambio la salvó».
teaching.explanationEs: Persuade = convencer a alguien de hacer algo.
segments: A story can also persuade, because the listener sees the result instead of
hearing an argument: 'Our shop nearly closed, until one change saved it.'
teaching.audioText: A story can also persuade, because the listener sees the result instead of hearing an argument: 'Our shop nearly closed, until one change saved it.'

teaching.en: After the setback, the lesson appears: 'That winter taught me to ask for help,' and one concrete image helps it resonate long after the talk.
teaching.es: Tras el revés aparece la lección: «Aquel invierno me enseñó a pedir ayuda», y una imagen concreta ayuda a que resuene mucho después de la charla.
teaching.explanationEs: Setback es un contratiempo; lesson casi siempre revela el propósito; resonate = calar.
segments: After the setback, the lesson appears: 'That winter taught me to ask for
help,' and one concrete image helps it resonate long after the talk.
teaching.audioText: After the setback, the lesson appears: 'That winter taught me to ask for help,' and one concrete image helps it resonate long after the talk.

teaching.en: Good speakers do not simply announce the moral: they drive the point home with one final sentence that tells the audience what to do next.
teaching.es: Los buenos oradores no se limitan a anunciar la moraleja: dejan clara la idea con una última frase que dice al público qué hacer a continuación.
teaching.explanationEs: Drive the point home = reforzar el mensaje hasta que no quepa duda.
segments: Good speakers do not simply announce the moral: they drive the point home
with one final sentence that tells the audience what to do next.
teaching.audioText: Good speakers do not simply announce the moral: they drive the point home with one final sentence that tells the audience what to do next.

prompt.es: Decide con qué propósito se cuenta esta historia.

choices.text: To warn the audience about what ignoring problems costs
To inspire the audience with a story of recovery
To persuade the audience to choose a local garage

feedback.es: El narrador muestra un error (ignorar el ruido) y lo que costó; no hay superación heroica ni un servicio que vender, así que la historia advierte.

hint.es: Fíjate en el error y en lo que cuesta.

origin.text: I ignored the noise in the engine for weeks. One night the car stopped on a dark road, forty miles from anywhere, and it took three hours before anyone came. Now I check everything before a long trip.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es decir, seguía el arco clásico de toda historia.»

feedback.es: El arco es la forma de la historia, de la situación inicial al desenlace pasando por el problema y el giro.

hint.es: Es la curva que va de la situación al desenlace.

origin.text: The anecdote began with a calm situation, introduced a problem in the second sentence and ended with a clear outcome. In other words, it followed the classic ___ of a story.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tras el revés, el equipo aprendió una dura lección.»

answer.text: After the setback the team learned a hard lesson

feedback.es: El revés va primero y la lección llega después: ese orden es el que revela el propósito de la historia.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla y elige con qué propósito y en qué momento se revela.

choices.text: To warn other bakers about supermarkets, because her own shop nearly closed.
To inspire the audience, and her final advice reveals the purpose.
To persuade people to shop locally, since her orders grew after the change.

feedback.es: Supera el revés del supermercado y termina con un consejo esperanzador; la frase final revela que busca inspirar, no advertir ni vender.

origin.audio: Last month a baker spoke at our community meeting. For years she opened at six, she said, and her bread was the best in the street. Then a supermarket opened next door, and her customers disappeared. She almost gave up. Instead, she began baking for neighbours who could not leave their homes, and within a year she had more orders than ever. She finished by saying, find the people who need you, and they will find you.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada historia breve con su propósito principal.

pairs: A nurse who kept going after failing her exam twice.
A man who lost his savings after ignoring every warning sign.
A school that cut waste by half, with figures for every month.
A list of dates with no problem and no lesson.

feedback.es: Cada historia destaca algo distinto: superar un revés, pagar un error, mostrar un resultado deseable o ningún propósito.

pairs: A nurse who kept going after failing her exam twice.
A man who lost his savings after ignoring every warning sign.
A school that cut waste by half, with figures for every month.
A list of dates with no problem and no lesson.

prompt.es: Elige el momento de la historia que revela su propósito.

choices.text: Then we moved online, and within a year we had customers in six countries.
Our shop was nearly empty, and the winter had been very long.
Today I tell every small business owner I meet: try something new.

feedback.es: La frase final se dirige al público y dice qué debe hacer: ahí se revela que el propósito es persuadir; lo anterior solo cuenta la situación y el desenlace.

origin.text: Our shop was nearly empty, and the winter had been very long. Then we moved online, and within a year we had customers in six countries. Today I tell every small business owner I meet: try something new before you have to.

prompt.es: Lee el final del discurso y elige qué pide realmente la directora a los asistentes.

choices.text: To build links with their neighbours before an emergency arrives.
To give money so that the library and the clinic can be built again.
To learn how to use a boat in case there is a flood.

feedback.es: Ella descarta expresamente la donación y pide conocer a los vecinos: lo que salvó al pueblo no fue el dinero sino las relaciones.

origin.text: When the flood came, we lost the library, the clinic and six years of records. What saved us was not money: it was the neighbours with boats. So I am not asking you for a donation tonight. I am asking you to learn the names of the people on your street.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la narradora guarda los formularios de los exámenes.

choices.text: They are proof that the test was stricter than it should have been.
They remind her that giving up would have been easier.
They show her sister how many attempts were needed.

feedback.es: Los guarda como recordatorio de que rendirse era lo fácil: es la lección que revela el propósito de inspirar.

origin.audio: I failed my driving test three times. The third time, the examiner looked at me and sighed. I remember thinking that I would never drive. But my sister said, one more try, and I booked it the same afternoon. I passed, hardly believing it. I still keep the failed forms in a drawer, because they remind me that quitting was always the easier choice.

prompt.es: Completa: «La frase final buscaba dejar clara la idea: nadie debe ignorar un aviso.»

feedback.es: Drive the point home es reforzar el mensaje hasta que no haya duda; aquí, con una frase final dirigida al público.

origin.text: The speaker told the story of the night the lights went out on the motorway. Her last sentence was meant to ___ the point home: nobody should ignore a warning light.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una historia con moraleja muestra un error y el precio que se paga.»

answer.text: A cautionary tale shows a mistake and the price that follows it

feedback.es: Un cautionary tale advierte mostrando el error y su precio, que es la estructura de este relato.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué propósito cuenta la mujer su historia de la empresa.

choices.text: To warn company owners about the risks of selling a business.
To celebrate how much the town loves its biggest company.
To persuade listeners that the same plan could work for them.

feedback.es: La frase final traslada el resultado al pueblo del oyente: el propósito es convencerle de que puede repetirse, no advertir ni criticar.

origin.audio: Everyone expected our town to lose its biggest company. Instead, the workers bought it. In the first year they lost money and nearly gave up. But they learned to sell directly to customers, and the company now gives jobs to two hundred people. If it worked here, I believe it can work in your town too.

prompt.es: Completa: «La historia resonó con el público porque todos habían vivido un revés así.»

feedback.es: Resonate con el público significa que la historia toca algo que los oyentes reconocen como propio.

origin.text: The outcome was not what they had hoped for, but the story still ___ with the audience because everyone in the room had faced a setback of some kind.

prompt.es: Lee la reseña y elige qué le reprocha el crítico a la oradora.

choices.text: That the story had no clear purpose or final lesson.
That she spent too long describing the loss of her business.
That she rushed the ending because the audience looked bored.

feedback.es: El crítico habla de una historia emotiva pero sin conclusión: no hubo lección ni petición, así que el público no supo qué se esperaba de él.

origin.text: The speaker told a moving story about losing her business, yet she offered no conclusion from it. We waited for the lesson; it never came. The audience left politely, without knowing what she wanted from them.
